tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before performing a move, verify that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg, that the source and destination pegs are different, and that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you propose a move, before adding it to the move list, check that it obeys all Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not on top of its source peg, moving a disk onto a smaller disk, or moving a disk to the same peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints; use it to temporarily hold space while moving larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks and you need a free peg to move the larger disk, move the smallest disk to an auxiliary peg first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a larger disk directly onto a peg that has a smaller disk on top, instead of moving the smallest disk away first.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and place smaller disks onto them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the destination peg already has a correctly ordered stack of larger disks, avoid moving them and instead stack the remaining disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk that is already correctly placed on the goal peg, thereby disturbing the correct order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto its goal peg in descending order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When building the final configuration, start with the largest disk and work downwards, ensuring each larger disk is placed before any smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing smaller disks before larger ones, resulting in an incorrect final ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, output it as the last syntactically correct list in the response, so the verifier can parse it correctly.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When finishing the solution, ensure the move list is the final element in the output and is syntactically correct.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the intended list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure source and destination pegs are clear of smaller disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk, make sure its source peg has no smaller disks on top and its destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger, so the move respects size ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is larger than some other disks, first relocate any smaller disks that block the source or destination.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a large disk onto a peg where a smaller disk sits on top, violating the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the output within token limits.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list, aim for the shortest correct sequence to avoid exceeding the model's output length constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing an overly long move list that gets truncated, resulting in an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the move list, mentally simulate each move on the initial configuration to ensure the final configuration exactly matches the goal; if any disk is misplaced, continue planning moves until the goal is reached.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the answer, run a mental simulation of the entire move sequence to confirm it achieves the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing a move list that stops early, leaving some disks not on the goal peg, so the final configuration differs from the target.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or assume no moves are needed when the initial state differs from the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always produce a move list; if the initial configuration is not already the goal, generate the necessary moves.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model fails to check the size constraint when selecting a destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk before committing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of the stack order on each peg and selects a disk that is buried under others.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit representation of each peg's stack and only select the topmost disk for any move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model reaches its token limit or stops generation before all necessary moves are produced.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating moves, simulate the final state; if the goal is not reached, continue planning additional moves until completion.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model mis‑identifies the current location of a disk, often due to an outdated or missing state representation.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep an up‑to‑date mapping of each disk to its current peg and verify presence before issuing a move.
